42 template <typename type>
43 using make_caster = type_caster<intrinsic_t<type>>;

45 // Shortcut for calling a caster's `cast_op_type` cast operator for casting a type_caster to a T
46 template <typename T>
47 typename make_caster<T>::template cast_op_type<T> cast_op(make_caster<T> &caster) {
48 using result_t = typename make_caster<T>::template cast_op_type<T>; // See PR #4893
49 return caster.operator result_t();

55 typename std::add_rvalue_reference<T>::type>; // See PR #4893
56 ✗ return std::move(caster).operator result_t();

89 ✗ if (native_enum) {

102 ✗ type_caster_base<EnumType> legacy_caster;
103 ✗ if (legacy_caster.load(src, convert)) {

107 ✗ return false;

131 struct type_caster_enum_type_enabled : std::true_type {};

133 template <typename T>
134 struct type_uses_type_caster_enum_type {
135 static constexpr bool value
136 = std::is_enum<T>::value && type_caster_enum_type_enabled<T>::value;
137 };

139 template <typename EnumType>
140 class type_caster<EnumType, detail::enable_if_t<type_uses_type_caster_enum_type<EnumType>::value>>
141 : public type_caster_enum_type<EnumType> {};

143 template <typename T, detail::enable_if_t<std::is_enum<T>::value, int> = 0>
144 bool isinstance_native_enum_impl(handle obj, const std::type_info &tp) {
145 handle native_enum = global_internals_native_enum_type_map_get_item(tp);
146 if (!native_enum) {
147 return false;
148 }
149 return isinstance(obj, native_enum);
150 }
151
152 template <typename T, detail::enable_if_t<!std::is_enum<T>::value, int> = 0>
153 bool isinstance_native_enum_impl(handle, const std::type_info &) {
154 return false;
155 }

501 "Unsupported char16_t size != 2");
502 static_assert(!std::is_same<CharT, char32_t>::value || sizeof(CharT) == 4,
503 "Unsupported char32_t size != 4");
504 // wchar_t can be either 16 bits (Windows) or 32 (everywhere else)
505 static_assert(!std::is_same<CharT, wchar_t>::value || sizeof(CharT) == 2 || sizeof(CharT) == 4,
506 "Unsupported wchar_t size != 2/4");

511 ✗ if (!src) {
512 ✗ return false;

521 ✗ Py_ssize_t size = -1;

523 ✗ = reinterpret_cast<const CharT *>(PyUnicode_AsUTF8AndSize(load_src.ptr(), &size));
524 ✗ if (!buffer) {
525 ✗ PyErr_Clear();
526 ✗ return false;

528 ✗ value = StringType(buffer, static_cast<size_t>(size));
529 ✗ return true;

534 UTF_N == 8 ? "utf-8"
535 : UTF_N == 16 ? "utf-16"
536 : "utf-32",
537 nullptr));

539 PyErr_Clear();
540 return false;
541 }

640 // Type caster for C-style strings. We basically use a std::string type caster, but also add the
641 // ability to use None as a nullptr char* (which the string caster doesn't allow).
642 template <typename CharT>
643 struct type_caster<CharT, enable_if_t<is_std_char_type<CharT>::value>> {
644 using StringType = std::basic_string<CharT>;
645 using StringCaster = make_caster<StringType>;
646 StringCaster str_caster;
647 bool none = false;
648 CharT one_char = 0;
649
650 public:
651 bool load(handle src, bool convert) {
652 if (!src) {
653 return false;
654 }
655 if (src.is_none()) {
656 // Defer accepting None to other overloads (if we aren't in convert mode):
657 if (!convert) {
658 return false;
659 }
660 none = true;
661 return true;
662 }
663 return str_caster.load(src, convert);
664 }
665
666 ✗ static handle cast(const CharT *src, return_value_policy policy, handle parent) {
667 ✗ if (src == nullptr) {
668 ✗ return pybind11::none().release();
669 }
670 ✗ return StringCaster::cast(StringType(src), policy, parent);
671 }
672
673 static handle cast(CharT src, return_value_policy policy, handle parent) {
674 if (std::is_same<char, CharT>::value) {
675 handle s = PyUnicode_DecodeLatin1((const char *) &src, 1, nullptr);
676 if (!s) {
677 throw error_already_set();
678 }
679 return s;
680 }
681 return StringCaster::cast(StringType(1, src), policy, parent);
682 }
683
684 explicit operator CharT *() {
685 return none ? nullptr : const_cast<CharT *>(static_cast<StringType &>(str_caster).c_str());
686 }
687 explicit operator CharT &() {
688 if (none) {
689 throw value_error("Cannot convert None to a character");
690 }
691
692 auto &value = static_cast<StringType &>(str_caster);
693 size_t str_len = value.size();
694 if (str_len == 0) {
695 throw value_error("Cannot convert empty string to a character");
696 }
697
698 // If we're in UTF-8 mode, we have two possible failures: one for a unicode character that
699 // is too high, and one for multiple unicode characters (caught later), so we need to
700 // figure out how long the first encoded character is in bytes to distinguish between these
701 // two errors. We also allow want to allow unicode characters U+0080 through U+00FF, as
702 // those can fit into a single char value.
703 if (StringCaster::UTF_N == 8 && str_len > 1 && str_len <= 4) {
704 auto v0 = static_cast<unsigned char>(value[0]);
705 // low bits only: 0-127
706 // 0b110xxxxx - start of 2-byte sequence
707 // 0b1110xxxx - start of 3-byte sequence
708 // 0b11110xxx - start of 4-byte sequence
709 size_t char0_bytes = (v0 & 0x80) == 0 ? 1
710 : (v0 & 0xE0) == 0xC0 ? 2
711 : (v0 & 0xF0) == 0xE0 ? 3
712 : 4;
713
714 if (char0_bytes == str_len) {
715 // If we have a 128-255 value, we can decode it into a single char:
716 if (char0_bytes == 2 && (v0 & 0xFC) == 0xC0) { // 0x110000xx 0x10xxxxxx
717 one_char = static_cast<CharT>(((v0 & 3) << 6)
718 + (static_cast<unsigned char>(value[1]) & 0x3F));
719 return one_char;
720 }
721 // Otherwise we have a single character, but it's > U+00FF
722 throw value_error("Character code point not in range(0x100)");
723 }
724 }
725
726 // UTF-16 is much easier: we can only have a surrogate pair for values above U+FFFF, thus a
727 // surrogate pair with total length 2 instantly indicates a range error (but not a "your
728 // string was too long" error).
729 else if (StringCaster::UTF_N == 16 && str_len == 2) {
730 one_char = static_cast<CharT>(value[0]);
731 if (one_char >= 0xD800 && one_char < 0xE000) {
732 throw value_error("Character code point not in range(0x10000)");
733 }
734 }
735
736 if (str_len != 1) {
737 throw value_error("Expected a character, but multi-character string found");
738 }
739
740 one_char = value[0];
741 return one_char;
742 }

745 template <typename _T>
746 using cast_op_type = pybind11::detail::cast_op_type<_T>;

780 auto h = cast(std::move(*src), policy, parent);
781 delete src;
782 return h;
783 }
784 return cast(*src, policy, parent);
785 }

787 static constexpr auto name = const_name("tuple[")
788 + ::pybind11::detail::concat(make_caster<Ts>::name...)
789 + const_name("]");
790
791 template <typename T>
792 using cast_op_type = type;
793
794 explicit operator type() & { return implicit_cast(indices{}); }
795 explicit operator type() && { return std::move(*this).implicit_cast(indices{}); }
796
797 protected:
798 template <size_t... Is>
799 type implicit_cast(index_sequence<Is...>) & {
800 return type(cast_op<Ts>(std::get<Is>(subcasters))...);
801 }
802 template <size_t... Is>
803 type implicit_cast(index_sequence<Is...>) && {
804 return type(cast_op<Ts>(std::move(std::get<Is>(subcasters)))...);
805 }
806
807 static constexpr bool load_impl(const sequence &, bool, index_sequence<>) { return true; }
808
809 template <size_t... Is>
810 bool load_impl(const sequence &seq, bool convert, index_sequence<Is...>) {
811 #ifdef __cpp_fold_expressions
812 if ((... || !std::get<Is>(subcasters).load(seq[Is], convert))) {
813 return false;
814 }
815 #else
816 for (bool r : {std::get<Is>(subcasters).load(seq[Is], convert)...}) {
817 if (!r) {
818 return false;
819 }
820 }
821 #endif
822 return true;
823 }

825 /* Implementation: Convert a C++ tuple into a Python tuple */
826 template <typename T, size_t... Is>
827 static handle
828 cast_impl(T &&src, return_value_policy policy, handle parent, index_sequence<Is...>) {
829 PYBIND11_WORKAROUND_INCORRECT_MSVC_C4100(src, policy, parent);
830 PYBIND11_WORKAROUND_INCORRECT_GCC_UNUSED_BUT_SET_PARAMETER(policy, parent);
831
832 std::array<object, size> entries{{reinterpret_steal<object>(
833 // NOLINTNEXTLINE(bugprone-use-after-move)
834 make_caster<Ts>::cast(std::get<Is>(std::forward<T>(src)), policy, parent))...}};
835 for (const auto &entry : entries) {
836 if (!entry) {
837 return handle();
838 }
839 }
840 tuple result(size);
841 int counter = 0;
842 for (auto &entry : entries) {
843 PyTuple_SET_ITEM(result.ptr(), counter++, entry.release().ptr());
844 }
845 return result.release();
846 }
847
848 Tuple<make_caster<Ts>...> subcasters;
849 };

864 /// Helper class which abstracts away certain actions. Users can provide specializations for
865 /// custom holders, but it's only necessary if the type has a non-standard interface.
866 template <typename T>
867 struct holder_helper {
868 static auto get(const T &p) -> decltype(p.get()) { return p.get(); }

871 // SMART_HOLDER_BAKEIN_FOLLOW_ON: Rewrite comment, with reference to shared_ptr specialization.
872 /// Type caster for holder types like std::shared_ptr, etc.
873 /// The SFINAE hook is provided to help work around the current lack of support
874 /// for smart-pointer interoperability. Please consider it an implementation
875 /// detail that may change in the future, as formal support for smart-pointer
876 /// interoperability is added into pybind11.
877 template <typename type, typename holder_type, typename SFINAE = void>
878 struct copyable_holder_caster : public type_caster_base<type> {
879 public:
880 using base = type_caster_base<type>;
881 static_assert(std::is_base_of<base, type_caster<type>>::value,
882 "Holder classes are only supported for custom types");

884 using base::cast;
885 using base::typeinfo;
886 using base::value;
887
888 bool load(handle src, bool convert) {
889 return base::template load_impl<copyable_holder_caster<type, holder_type>>(src, convert);
890 }
891

893 // static_cast works around compiler error with MSVC 17 and CUDA 10.2
894 // see issue #2180
895 explicit operator type &() { return *(static_cast<type *>(this->value)); }
896 explicit operator holder_type *() { return std::addressof(holder); }
897 explicit operator holder_type &() { return holder; }
898
899 static handle cast(const holder_type &src, return_value_policy, handle) {
900 const auto *ptr = holder_helper<holder_type>::get(src);
901 return type_caster_base<type>::cast_holder(ptr, &src);
902 }

904 protected:
905 friend class type_caster_generic;
906 void check_holder_compat() {
907 // SMART_HOLDER_BAKEIN_FOLLOW_ON: Refine holder compatibility checks.
908 bool inst_has_unique_ptr_holder
909 = (typeinfo->holder_enum_v == holder_enum_t::std_unique_ptr);
910 if (inst_has_unique_ptr_holder) {
911 throw cast_error("Unable to load a custom holder type from a default-holder instance");
912 }
913 }
914
915 bool set_foreign_holder(handle src) {
916 return holder_caster_foreign_helpers::set_foreign_holder(src, (type *) value, &holder);
917 }
918
919 void load_value(value_and_holder &&v_h) {
920 if (v_h.holder_constructed()) {
921 value = v_h.value_ptr();
922 holder = v_h.template holder<holder_type>();
923 return;
924 }
925 throw cast_error("Unable to cast from non-held to held instance (T& to Holder<T>) "
926 #if !defined(PYBIND11_DETAILED_ERROR_MESSAGES)
927 "(#define PYBIND11_DETAILED_ERROR_MESSAGES or compile in debug mode for "
928 "type information)");
929 #else
930 "of type '"
931 + type_id<holder_type>() + "''");
932 #endif
933 }
934
935 template <typename T = holder_type,
936 detail::enable_if_t<!std::is_constructible<T, const T &, type *>::value, int> = 0>
937 bool try_implicit_casts(handle, bool) {
938 return false;
939 }
940
941 template <typename T = holder_type,
942 detail::enable_if_t<std::is_constructible<T, const T &, type *>::value, int> = 0>
943 bool try_implicit_casts(handle src, bool convert) {
944 for (auto &cast : typeinfo->implicit_casts) {
945 copyable_holder_caster sub_caster(*cast.first);
946 if (sub_caster.load(src, convert)) {
947 value = cast.second(sub_caster.value);
948 holder = holder_type(sub_caster.holder, (type *) value);
949 return true;
950 }
951 }
952 return false;
953 }
954
955 static bool try_direct_conversions(handle) { return false; }
956
957 holder_type holder;
958 };

1115 /// Return a std::shared_ptr with the SAME CONTROL BLOCK as the std::shared_ptr owned by the
1116 /// class_ holder. For class_-wrapped types with trampolines, the returned std::shared_ptr
1117 /// does NOT keep any derived Python objects alive (see issue #1333).
1118 ///
1119 /// For class_-wrapped types using std::shared_ptr as the holder, the following expressions
1120 /// produce equivalent results (see tests/test_potentially_slicing_weak_ptr.cpp,py):
1121 ///
1122 /// - obj.cast<std::shared_ptr<T>>()
1123 /// - py::potentially_slicing_weak_ptr<T>(obj).lock()
1124 ///
1125 /// For class_-wrapped types with trampolines and using py::smart_holder, obj.cast<>()
1126 /// produces a std::shared_ptr that keeps any derived Python objects alive for its own lifetime,
1127 /// but this is achieved by introducing a std::shared_ptr control block that is independent of
1128 /// the one owned by the py::smart_holder. This can lead to surprising std::weak_ptr behavior
1129 /// (see issue #5623). An easy solution is to use py::potentially_slicing_weak_ptr<>(obj),
1130 /// as exercised in tests/test_potentially_slicing_weak_ptr.cpp,py (look for
1131 /// "set_wp_potentially_slicing"). Note, however, that this reintroduces the inheritance
1132 /// slicing issue (see issue #1333). The ideal — but usually more involved — solution is to use
1133 /// a Python weakref to the derived Python object, instead of a C++ base-class std::weak_ptr.
1134 ///
1135 /// It is not possible (at least no known approach exists at the time of this writing) to
1136 /// simultaneously achieve both desirable properties:
1137 ///
1138 /// - the same std::shared_ptr control block as the class_ holder
1139 /// - automatic lifetime extension of any derived Python objects
1140 ///
1141 /// The reason is that this would introduce a reference cycle that cannot be garbage collected:
1142 ///
1143 /// - the derived Python object owns the class_ holder
1144 /// - the class_ holder owns the std::shared_ptr
1145 /// - the std::shared_ptr would own a reference to the derived Python object,
1146 /// completing the cycle
1147 template <typename T>
1148 std::weak_ptr<T> potentially_slicing_weak_ptr(handle obj) {
1149 detail::make_caster<std::shared_ptr<T>> caster;
1150 if (caster.load(obj, /*convert=*/true)) {
1151 return caster.potentially_slicing_weak_ptr();
1152 }
1153 const char *obj_type_name = detail::obj_class_name(obj.ptr());
1154 throw type_error("\"" + std::string(obj_type_name)
1155 + "\" object is not convertible to std::weak_ptr<T> (with T = " + type_id<T>()
1156 + ")");
1157 }
1158
1159 PYBIND11_NAMESPACE_BEGIN(detail)

1164 /// in the comment for the copyable_holder_caster.

1168 "Holder classes are only supported for custom types");

1516 template <typename type>
1517 struct pyobject_caster {
1518 template <typename T = type, enable_if_t<std::is_same<T, handle>::value, int> = 0>
1519 ✗ pyobject_caster() : value() {}

1521 // `type` may not be default constructible (e.g. frozenset, anyset). Initializing `value`
1522 // to a nil handle is safe since it will only be accessed if `load` succeeds.
1523 template <typename T = type, enable_if_t<std::is_base_of<object, T>::value, int> = 0>
1524 ✗ pyobject_caster() : value(reinterpret_steal<type>(handle())) {}
1525
1526 template <typename T = type, enable_if_t<std::is_same<T, handle>::value, int> = 0>
1527 ✗ bool load(handle src, bool /* convert */) {
1528 ✗ value = src;
1529 ✗ return static_cast<bool>(value);
1530 }
1531
1532 template <typename T = type, enable_if_t<std::is_base_of<object, T>::value, int> = 0>
1533 ✗ bool load(handle src, bool /* convert */) {
1534 ✗ if (!isinstance<type>(src)) {
1535 ✗ return false;
1536 }
1537 ✗ value = reinterpret_borrow<type>(src);
1538 ✗ return true;
1539 }
1540
1541 ✗ static handle cast(const handle &src, return_value_policy /* policy */, handle /* parent */) {
1542 ✗ return src.inc_ref();
1543 }
1544 ✗ PYBIND11_TYPE_CASTER(type, handle_type_name<type>::name);

1550 template <>
1551 class type_caster<float_> : public pyobject_caster<float_> {
1552 public:
1553 bool load(handle src, bool /* convert */) {
1554 if (isinstance<float_>(src)) {
1555 value = reinterpret_borrow<float_>(src);
1556 } else if (isinstance<int_>(src)) {
1557 value = float_(reinterpret_borrow<int_>(src));
1558 } else {
1559 return false;
1560 }
1561 return true;
1562 }
1563 };

1565 // Our conditions for enabling moving are quite restrictive:
1566 // At compile time:
1567 // - T needs to be a non-const, non-pointer, non-reference type
1568 // - type_caster<T>::operator T&() must exist
1569 // - the type must be move constructible (obviously)
1570 // At run-time:
1571 // - if the type is non-copy-constructible, the object must be the sole owner of the type (i.e. it
1572 // must have ref_count() == 1)h
1573 // If any of the above are not satisfied, we fall back to copying.
1574 template <typename T>
1575 using move_is_plain_type
1576 = satisfies_none_of<T, std::is_void, std::is_pointer, std::is_reference, std::is_const>;
1577 template <typename T, typename SFINAE = void>
1578 struct move_always : std::false_type {};
1579 template <typename T>
1580 struct move_always<
1581 T,
1582 enable_if_t<
1583 all_of<move_is_plain_type<T>,
1584 negation<is_copy_constructible<T>>,
1585 is_move_constructible<T>,
1586 std::is_same<decltype(std::declval<make_caster<T>>().operator T &()), T &>>::value>>
1587 : std::true_type {};
1588 template <typename T, typename SFINAE = void>
1589 struct move_if_unreferenced : std::false_type {};
1590 template <typename T>
1591 struct move_if_unreferenced<
1592 T,
1593 enable_if_t<
1594 all_of<move_is_plain_type<T>,
1595 negation<move_always<T>>,
1596 is_move_constructible<T>,
1597 std::is_same<decltype(std::declval<make_caster<T>>().operator T &()), T &>>::value>>
1598 : std::true_type {};
1599 template <typename T>
1600 using move_never = none_of<move_always<T>, move_if_unreferenced<T>>;

1602 // Detect whether returning a `type` from a cast on type's type_caster is going to result in a
1603 // reference or pointer to a local variable of the type_caster. Basically, only
1604 // non-reference/pointer `type`s and reference/pointers from a type_caster_generic are safe;
1605 // everything else returns a reference/pointer to a local variable.
1606 template <typename type>
1607 using cast_is_temporary_value_reference
1608 = bool_constant<(std::is_reference<type>::value || std::is_pointer<type>::value)
1609 && !std::is_base_of<type_caster_generic, make_caster<type>>::value
1610 && !std::is_same<intrinsic_t<type>, void>::value>;
1611
1612 // When a value returned from a C++ function is being cast back to Python, we almost always want to
1613 // force `policy = move`, regardless of the return value policy the function/method was declared
1614 // with.
1615 template <typename Return, typename SFINAE = void>
1616 struct return_value_policy_override {
1617 ✗ static return_value_policy policy(return_value_policy p) { return p; }
1618 };
1619
1620 template <typename Return>
1621 struct return_value_policy_override<
1622 Return,
1623 detail::enable_if_t<std::is_base_of<type_caster_generic, make_caster<Return>>::value, void>> {
1624 ✗ static return_value_policy policy(return_value_policy p) {
1625 return !std::is_lvalue_reference<Return>::value && !std::is_pointer<Return>::value
1626 ? return_value_policy::move
1627 ✗ : p;
1628 }
1629 };

1689 // Note that `cast<PyObject *>(obj)` increments the reference count of `obj`.
1690 // This is necessary for the case that `obj` is a temporary, and could
1691 // not possibly be different, given

1693 // 2. we don't want to force all generic code using `cast<T>()` to special-case
1694 // handling of `T` = `PyObject *` (to increment the reference count there).
1695 // It is the responsibility of the caller to ensure that the reference count
1696 // is decremented.

1700 && detail::is_same_ignoring_cvref<Handle, handle>::value,

1704 return handle.inc_ref().ptr();

1710 && detail::is_same_ignoring_cvref<Object, object>::value,

1712 = 0>
